Definition: from G4141; a stroke; by implication, a wound; figuratively, a calamity:--plague, stripe, wound(-ed).
BiblicalUsage: Plege is a blow, a wound, a plague — a stroke that leaves a mark. The man on the Jericho road was left wounded in Luke 10:30, and Paul and Silas were laid with many stripes in Acts 16:23. Paul counts stripes among his sufferings in 2 Corinthians 6:5, and Revelation 16:21 says the plague of hail was exceeding great.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God counts every stripe His servants bear, and every plague He sends is measured. That is why I hold that wounds for His sake are never wasted.
